title: 집 · 거주지
intro: OPIc 설문에서 거의 항상 출제되는 핵심 주제로, 집 묘사 → 집에서의 일상 → 집과 관련된 경험(고장·문제) → 예전 집과 비교 순서로 나옵니다. 모든 답변은 '회사 근처 아파트 7층, 방 1개짜리(거실 겸 부엌, 침실), 화분이 있는 작은 발코니, 3년 전 취업하며 이사해 혼자 거주'라는 하나의 집으로 통일하세요. 비교 질문에는 대학 시절까지 가족과 살던 대전의 오래된 아파트를 쓰면 자기소개 내용과 그대로 이어집니다.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 'Okay, let me tell you about my place.' → 집 기본 정보(아파트 7층, 방 1개, 혼자) → 공간 묘사(거실 겸 부엌 → 침실 → 발코니) → 좋아하는 공간과 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
묘사는 현관에서 안쪽으로 공간 순서대로 이동하면 길을 잃지 않아요. 'When you walk in, ~' / 'Next to ~, there's ~'.
혼자 사는 직장인이라는 설정을 살려 '내 공간', '퇴근 후 쉬는 곳', '집안일을 혼자 다 한다' 같은 느낌과 이유를 붙이면 IH 이상이 됩니다.
비교 질문은 대전 본가(가족과 살던 넓고 오래된 아파트) vs 지금 집(작지만 새롭고 회사와 가까움)으로 차이 2가지와 느낌을 말합니다.

expressions.en: Okay, let me tell you about my place.
expressions.ko: 네, 제 집에 대해 말해 볼게요.
expressions.note: 시작 문장. my place = 우리 집 (구어체)

expressions.en: I live in an apartment near my office.
I live alone, so it's just me.
My apartment is on the seventh floor.
The living room and the kitchen are in one space.
There's a small balcony with some plants.
expressions.ko: 화분 몇 개가 있는 작은 발코니가 있어요.

expressions.en: My favorite spot is the sofa in the living room.
expressions.ko: 제가 제일 좋아하는 곳은 거실 소파예요.

expressions.en: I moved here about three years ago when I got my job.
expressions.note: when I got my job: 취직했을 때

expressions.en: It's not very big, but it's really cozy.
expressions.note: not ~, but ~: 단점 뒤에 장점으로 대조

expressions.en: Since I live alone, I have to do all the housework myself.
expressions.ko: 혼자 살아서 집안일을 전부 직접 해야 해요.

expressions.en: The best thing about my place is that it's close to work.
expressions.ko: 우리 집의 제일 좋은 점은 회사와 가깝다는 거예요.
expressions.note: The best thing about ~ is that ~

expressions.en: Yeah, that's pretty much what my place looks like.
expressions.ko: 네, 우리 집은 대충 이렇게 생겼어요.

expressions.en: It's a lot smaller than my parents' place, but it's all mine.
expressions.ko: 부모님 집보다 훨씬 작지만, 온전히 제 공간이에요.

expressions.en: After a long day at work, nothing beats coming home to my own little space.
expressions.ko: 회사에서 긴 하루를 보낸 뒤 나만의 작은 공간으로 돌아오는 것만큼 좋은 게 없어요.

questions.en: I'd like to know about where you live. Can you describe your home? What does it look like, and how many rooms does it have?
questions.ko: 어디에 사는지 알고 싶어요. 집을 묘사해 주시겠어요? 어떻게 생겼고, 방은 몇 개인가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 집 기본 정보(아파트 7층, 방 1개, 혼자) → 거실 겸 부엌 → 침실 → 발코니 → 좋아하는 공간 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
공간 순서대로 이동하며 'When you walk in, ~', 'Next to ~' 표현을 쓰세요.
'It's not very big, but it's really cozy.'처럼 느낌 한 줄을 꼭 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about my place. I live in an apartment near my office. I live alone, so it's just me. My apartment is on the seventh floor. It's a one-bedroom apartment. The living room and the kitchen are in one space. My bedroom is small, but it's cozy. There's also a small balcony with some plants. My favorite spot is the sofa in the living room. Yeah, that's my home.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you about my place. I live alone in an apartment near my office. I moved here about three years ago when I got my job. It's on the seventh floor, and it's a one-bedroom apartment. When you walk in, there's the living room, and the kitchen is in the same space. I have a gray sofa, a TV, and a small table there. My bedroom is next to the living room. It has a bed, a desk, and a big closet. There's also a small balcony with some plants, and I water them every weekend. My place is not very big, but it's really cozy. My favorite spot is the sofa, because I watch movies there on Friday nights. The best thing about my place is that it's close to work. Yeah, that's pretty much what my place looks like.
answers.AL: Okay, let me tell you about my place. I live alone in a one-bedroom apartment on the seventh floor, just a short subway ride from my office. I moved in about three years ago when I got my job, so it's the first place that's really mine. When you walk in, the first thing you see is the living room, which also works as the kitchen. It's an open space with a gray sofa, a TV, and a small dining table by the window. I'll be honest, I don't cook anything fancy, but I love making a simple dinner and eating it there. Next to the living room is my bedroom. It's pretty simple, just a bed, a desk, and a closet that's way too full of clothes. And then there's my favorite little corner, the balcony. It's tiny, but I've filled it with plants, and on weekend mornings, I sit out there with a cup of coffee. My place isn't big at all, but it's bright and cozy, and it feels like me. After a long day at work, nothing beats coming home to my own little space. Yeah, that's pretty much what my place looks like.

questions.en: What do you usually do at home? Tell me about a typical day at your home from morning to night.
questions.ko: 집에서 주로 무엇을 하나요? 아침부터 밤까지 집에서의 일상을 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 아침(출근 준비) → 퇴근 후 저녁 → 밤(영화·휴식) → 재택근무 날·주말 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
평일 기준으로 말하고, 금요일 재택근무나 주말 집안일을 덧붙이면 내용이 풍부해집니다.
혼자 살기 때문에 'I cook for myself', 'I do the laundry' 같은 집안일 표현을 쓰기 좋아요.

answers.IM3: Sure, I'd love to talk about my day at home. In the morning, I get up at seven thirty. I take a shower and eat some toast. Then I go to work. I come home around seven. I cook a simple dinner for myself. After dinner, I wash the dishes. Then I relax on the sofa and watch Netflix. On weekends, I clean my apartment and do the laundry. Yeah, that's what I usually do at home.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about what I do at home. On weekdays, I get up at seven thirty and get ready for work. I usually have toast and coffee at my small table by the window. I come home around seven, and since I live alone, I cook dinner for myself. It's usually something easy, like pasta or kimchi fried rice. After I wash the dishes, I relax on the sofa and watch Netflix or listen to music. Fridays are a little different, because I work from home. I set up my laptop at the table, and I can work in comfortable clothes, which I love. On Friday nights, I always watch a movie. On weekends, I clean my apartment, do the laundry, and water the plants on my balcony. Yeah, that's pretty much what I do at home.
answers.AL: Sure, I'd love to talk about what I do at home. On weekdays, my mornings are pretty simple. I get up at seven thirty, take a quick shower, and have toast and coffee at the little table by the window. Since I live alone, it's always quiet, and I actually like starting the day that way. I get home from work around seven, and the first thing I do is change into comfortable clothes. Then I cook something easy for dinner, like pasta or kimchi fried rice. I'm not a great cook, but it's way cheaper than eating out every night. After I do the dishes, I finally get to relax. I usually lie on the sofa and watch an episode of a show, or I put on some IU songs and read a little. Fridays feel a bit special, because I work from home. I set up my laptop at the table, and I don't have to deal with the subway at all. Then on Friday night, I treat myself to a movie and some snacks. On weekends, I catch up on chores, like cleaning, doing the laundry, and watering the plants on my balcony. Yeah, that's pretty much what a day at my place looks like.

questions.en: Have you ever had a problem at your home, like something breaking? Tell me what happened and how you handled it.
questions.ko: 집에서 뭔가 고장 나는 등 문제가 생긴 적이 있나요? 무슨 일이 있었고 어떻게 해결했는지 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·무엇이 고장 났는지 → 처음 느낌·어려움 → 어떻게 해결했는지 → 배운 점·느낌 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
과거 경험이므로 과거 시제(broke, called, came)를 일관되게 쓰세요.
혼자 살아서 직접 해결해야 했다는 점을 강조하면 이야기에 감정이 생깁니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, a problem at home? Let me think. Yes, last winter, my boiler broke. It was a really cold night. There was no hot water, and my apartment was freezing. I live alone, so I didn't know what to do. I called the building manager. He gave me a repairman's number. The repairman came the next morning and fixed it. I had to wear two sweaters to bed that night. Yeah, that was a really tough night.
answers.IH: Oh, a problem at home? Let me think. Yes, I had one last winter. One night in January, I came home from work, and my apartment was really cold. I checked the boiler, and it wasn't working at all. There was no hot water, either. Since I live alone, I had to handle it by myself, and honestly, I was a little scared. First, I called the building manager. He told me it was too late for a repairman, so I had to wait until the next morning. That night, I wore two sweaters and slept under three blankets. In the morning, I asked my team leader if I could start work a little late. The repairman came at eight and fixed the boiler in about an hour. After that, I saved his number on my phone. Yeah, that's the story of my freezing night.
answers.AL: Oh, a problem at home? Let me think. Yeah, there's one I'll never forget. It was a freezing night last January. I got home from work around eight, and the second I opened the door, I could tell something was wrong. My apartment was ice cold. I checked the boiler, and it was completely dead. No heat, no hot water, nothing. When you live alone, there's nobody else to fix things, so I really had to figure it out myself. First, I called the building manager, but he said it was too late to get a repairman that night. So I put on two sweaters, made some hot tea, and slept under every blanket I owned. I even thought about calling my parents in Daejeon, but I didn't want them to worry. The next morning, I texted my team leader that I'd be a little late. Luckily, the repairman showed up at eight and fixed it in about an hour. It turned out one part was just old. Looking back, it was kind of funny, but it also taught me a lot. Now I keep the repairman's number on my fridge, just in case. Yeah, that's the story of my coldest night at home.

questions.en: How is the home you live in now different from the home you lived in when you were a child?
questions.ko: 지금 사는 집은 어릴 때 살던 집과 어떻게 다른가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 예전 집(대전, 가족과 살던 오래된 아파트) → 지금 집(서울, 혼자 사는 작은 아파트) → 차이점 2가지 → 어느 쪽이 좋은지와 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~' 마무리
비교급(bigger, newer, quieter)과 'On the other hand, ~'로 대조하세요.
예전 집은 과거 시제(used to, had), 지금 집은 현재 시제로 구분하세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, that's a good question. When I was a child, I lived with my family in Daejeon. It was an old apartment with three bedrooms. It was big, but everything was a little old. Now, I live alone in Seoul. My apartment is much smaller. It only has one bedroom. But it's newer and cleaner. Also, it's really close to my office. I miss my family sometimes, though. Yeah, that's the difference between my two homes.
answers.IH: Oh, that's a good question. When I was a child, I lived with my family in Daejeon. I lived there until I finished college. It was an old apartment with three bedrooms, so it was much bigger than my place now. I had my own room, but I always fought with my brother Junho over the bathroom. Now, I live alone in a one-bedroom apartment in Seoul. It's a lot smaller, but it's newer and cleaner, and it's only 15 minutes from my office. Another big difference is the atmosphere. My parents' home was always noisy and warm, because my mom was always cooking something. My place now is really quiet. Sometimes I feel a little lonely, but I love having my own space. Yeah, that's how my two homes are different.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a good question. When I was a child, I lived with my parents and my younger brother Junho in Daejeon. We lived in the same old apartment until I finished college, so most of my memories are from that place. It had three bedrooms and a big living room, but everything was kind of worn out, like the old wallpaper and the squeaky doors. The home I live in now is pretty much the opposite. It's a one-bedroom apartment in Seoul, so it's way smaller, but it's newer, brighter, and just 15 minutes from my office. The biggest difference, though, is the feeling. My parents' place was always loud and full of life. My mom was always cooking something, and Junho and I used to fight over the bathroom every morning. Now, when I come home, it's completely quiet. To be honest, it felt a little lonely when I first moved in. But over time, I've come to love the freedom. I can decorate the way I want, eat whenever I want, and watch movies as late as I like. I still miss my mom's cooking, though, so I go back to Daejeon during the holidays. Yeah, that's how my two homes are different.
